facts.fact: The first Andhra Mahasabha met in 1913 at Bapatla.
The Telugu districts lay in the Madras Presidency.
A separate Andhra Congress unit followed in 1917.
The Sri Bagh Pact (1937) was between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
It was signed at Sri Bagh, the Madras home of Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao.
The Dhar Commission (1948) and JVP Committee (1949) advised against immediate linguistic states.
Potti Sriramulu began his final fast on 19 October 1952.
He died on 15 December 1952.
Potti Sriramulu's fast-unto-death triggered Andhra State.
Nehru announced Andhra State on 19 December 1952.
Parliament passed the Andhra State Act in 1953.
Potti Sriramulu is called 'Amarajeevi'.
Andhra State (1 Oct 1953) had its capital at Kurnool.
Andhra State comprised 11 districts.
The High Court of Andhra State was at Guntur.
Tanguturi Prakasam ('Andhra Kesari') was the first CM of Andhra State.
Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last CM of Andhra State.
Andhra State was the first state formed on a linguistic basis.
The SRC (1953) was chaired by Fazl Ali.
H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were members of the SRC.
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised states largely on language.
'Visalandhra' meant a united state of all Telugu-speaking people.
The Gentlemen's Agreement (1956) gave safeguards to Telangana.
Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956.
Hyderabad became the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh.
The Mulki rules gave residence-based preference for local jobs and admissions.
The 1969 Telangana agitation was led by the Telangana Praja Samithi under Marri Chenna Reddy.
The Jai Andhra movement (1972) followed the Supreme Court upholding the Mulki rules.
The Six-Point Formula (1973) was implemented through Article 371-D.
Article 371-D came through the 32nd Amendment.
Causes of the Telangana demand included breach of safeguards and concentration of development around Hyderabad.
The demand revived under the TRS of K. Chandrashekar Rao.
The Srikrishna Committee (2010) examined the Telangana demand.
The appointed day for Telangana was 2 June 2014; it became the 29th state.
Hyderabad was made the common capital for up to ten years.
Amaravati was planned as the capital of residuary Andhra Pradesh.
AP was reorganised into 26 districts on 4 April 2022.
Polavaram and Markapuram made 28 districts on 31 December 2025.
Rampachodavaram is the headquarters of Polavaram district.
Madanapalle is the headquarters of Annamayya district, not a district itself.
AP's 28 zilla parishads take effect from 25 September 2026.
The first Andhra Mahasabha met at Bapatla on 26 May 1913 under the presidency of Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma.
The second Andhra Mahasabha met at Bezawada (Vijayawada) in 1914 under Nyapati Subba Rao Pantulu.
The demand for a separate Andhra province is usually dated from 1911–12, when Telugu leaders and papers first raised it.
The Nagpur Congress (1920) reorganised the Congress on linguistic provinces, giving Andhra its own Pradesh Congress unit.
Andhra University was founded in 1926 (first at Bezawada, moved to Waltair in 1930); C.R. Reddy was its first Vice-Chancellor.
The name 'Rayalaseema' for the Ceded Districts was coined by Chilukuri Narayana Rao at the Nandyal conference (1928).
In 1938 the Madras Legislative Assembly passed a resolution, moved by Konda Venkatappayya, for separate Andhra and Kerala provinces.
The JVP Report (April 1949) agreed to an Andhra State only if the Andhras gave up their claim to Madras city.
A Partition Committee of the Madras government (1949) on separating Andhra deadlocked over Madras city; Prakasam dissented.
Swami Sitaram (Gollapudi Sitarama Sastry) fasted for 35 days in 1951 for Andhra State and broke it at Vinoba Bhave's appeal.
The Sri Bagh Pact was signed on 16 November 1937.
Its signatories included Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Kadapa Koti Reddy.
The Pact promised an Andhra University centre at Anantapur for Rayalaseema.
It gave Rayalaseema priority in irrigation projects such as Tungabhadra and Krishna–Pennar for ten years.
Rayalaseema was given the choice of the capital or the High Court, the other going to the coast.
Legislative seats were to be distributed district-wise on an equal basis between the two regions.
Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in Madras; his family came from Padamatipalli in Nellore district.
In 1946 he fasted for the entry of Dalits into the Venugopalaswamy temple at Nellore.
He fasted at Bulusu Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore, Madras.
His last fast lasted 58 days (19 October – 15 December 1952).
Nellore district was renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district in 2008.
Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed (December 1952) to report on the financial and administrative implications of forming Andhra State.
Nehru inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool on 1 October 1953.
C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra State (and later of Andhra Pradesh).
The Andhra High Court opened at Guntur in July 1954 with Koka Subba Rao as its first Chief Justice.
The 11 districts were Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Nellore, Kurnool, Anantapur, Cuddapah and Chittoor.
Bellary town and its surrounding taluks went to Mysore, not Andhra, after the Misra report (1953).
Prakasam's ministry fell by one vote in November 1954; after President's Rule and the 1955 election Bezawada Gopala Reddy became Chief Minister.
Nallapati Venkatramaiah was the first Speaker of the Andhra State Legislative Assembly.
Puchalapalli Sundarayya's book 'Visalandhralo Prajarajyam' (1946) gave the Communists' case for Visalandhra.
The SRC recommended that Telangana stay a separate Hyderabad State, merging with Andhra after the 1961 elections only if two-thirds of its legislators agreed.
Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Chief Minister of Hyderabad State (1952–56), backed the merger.
The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed in Delhi on 20 February 1956.
Bezawada Gopala Reddy, Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy, Gouthu Latchanna and Alluri Satyanarayana Raju signed for Andhra; Burgula, K.V. Ranga Reddy, Marri Chenna Reddy and J.V. Narsing Rao for Telangana.
The Agreement provided that if the Chief Minister came from Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister would be from Telangana (and vice versa).
It required 12 years' residence in Telangana for local job preference.
A Telangana Regional Council (implemented as the Regional Committee, 1958, under Article 371) was to supervise development, education and jobs in Telangana.
The Mulki rules of the Nizam (1919) defined a local as one resident for 15 years.
Nehru likened the 1956 merger to a 'matrimonial alliance' with provision for divorce if the partners could not get along.
Andhra Pradesh began on 1 November 1956 with 20 districts — 11 from Andhra and 9 from Telangana.
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
The Pataskar award moved Tiruttani to Madras and gave Andhra Pradesh areas in Chittoor (boundary Act 1959, effective 1960).
The 1969 agitation began in January 1969 with a fast by a student, Ravindranath, at Khammam.
Indira Gandhi's Eight-Point Plan (April 1969) failed to end the Telangana agitation.
The Telangana Praja Samithi won 10 of the 14 Lok Sabha seats in Telangana in 1971 and then merged with the Congress.
P.V. Narasimha Rao, from Telangana, became Chief Minister in 1971 and resigned in January 1973 during the Jai Andhra agitation.
The Supreme Court upheld the Mulki rules on 3 October 1972.
Kakani Venkataratnam, a minister who led the Jai Andhra movement, died during the agitation (December 1972).
President's Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh from January to December 1973.
The Six-Point Formula was announced on 21 September 1973.
The 32nd Amendment (1973) inserted Article 371-D and Article 371-E; under 371-E the University of Hyderabad (1974) was set up.
The Presidential Order of 1975 under Article 371-D created local cadres and six zones for public employment.
G.O. 610 (1985) ordered repatriation of non-local employees posted in Telangana; the Girglani Commission (2001) found its violation.
K. Chandrashekar Rao founded the Telangana Rashtra Samithi on 27 April 2001.
KCR began a fast on 29 November 2009; on 9 December 2009 Home Minister P. Chidambaram announced that the formation of Telangana would be initiated.
The Srikrishna Committee (Justice B.N. Srikrishna), set up in February 2010, reported on 30 December 2010 with six options.
The Congress Working Committee resolved to form Telangana on 30 July 2013.
N. Kiran Kumar Reddy, the last Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh, resigned in February 2014; President's Rule followed until June 2014.
K. Chandrashekar Rao became the first CM of Telangana (2 June 2014) and N. Chandrababu Naidu the first CM of residuary AP (8 June 2014).
Seven mandals of Khammam (Bhadrachalam area) to be submerged by Polavaram were transferred to AP in 2014.
The AP Reorganisation Act 2014 declared Polavaram a national project.
PM Modi laid the foundation stone of Amaravati at Uddandarayunipalem on 22 October 2015.
A separate High Court of Andhra Pradesh began functioning at Amaravati on 1 January 2019.
The 2020 decentralisation Act proposed three capitals — Visakhapatnam (executive), Amaravati (legislative), Kurnool (judicial) — and was repealed in November 2021.
Hyderabad's ten-year term as common capital ended on 2 June 2024.
